soldier: Soldier: the head shape varies markedly, two forms, elongate-oval and nearly circular, occurring in the same colony, elongate-oval individuals making up about 80 per cent. In circular individuals the head is short and broad and the postmentum distinctly shorter, the remaining characters differing little. Head, antennae and labrum pale yellow, the antennal carinae and fontanelle tube reddish brown, mandibles reddish brown, legs and abdomen pale white. The head with scattered long and short hairs, the sides of the fontanelle with two long bristles each; the labrum, besides two apical hairs, often with lateral-apical hairs and disc hairs; the pronotum with more bristles than the head, the bristles of the abdominal tergites rather dense. The elongate-oval head is mostly widest at the basal third, the circular head widest at the middle. Fontanelle aperture oval, projecting as a short tube, the aperture not visible in dorsal view, in profile slightly approaching vertical. Mandibles sickle-shaped, their tips curved inwards, the base of the left mandible with three to four serrations, increasing in size from front to back. Labrum like an equilateral triangle, slightly longer than wide or almost equal, its transparent tip projecting as a point. Antennae with 15–16 segments, mostly 15, the third short and small. In the elongate-oval form the postmentum is rather short, the waist between the widest part and the posterior margin; in the circular form the postmentum is shorter still and the waist near the posterior end. The middle of the anterior margin of the pronotum is slightly concave, the middle of the posterior margin indistinctly concave.
